ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the comparative form of 'tall'? (1 mark)
   A. tallr
   B. tallest
   C. taller
   D. more tall

2. Which word helps to show order in a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. eleven
   B. table
   C. blue
   D. suddenly

3. In the story shape, the highest point is (1 mark)
   A. the title
   B. the last full stop
   C. the exciting part
   D. the date

4. 'There are ___ books on the desk.' Which fits a positive statement? (1 mark)
   A. how
   B. any
   C. some
   D. much

5. In a picture series, which picture usually shows the ending? (1 mark)
   A. The first picture
   B. The middle picture
   C. The last picture
   D. None of them

6. Which word contains the sound /ɛə/? (1 mark)
   A. chin
   B. chop
   C. chair
   D. chest

7. Which sentence talks about a finished action in the past? (1 mark)
   A. Kamau buys data bundles every week.
   B. Kamau bought data bundles yesterday.
   C. Kamau will buy data bundles tomorrow.
   D. Kamau is buying data bundles now.

8. Why is it good to write new words and meanings in a notebook while reading? (1 mark)
   A. It is required by law
   B. It makes the book shorter
   C. It replaces reading
   D. It helps you remember them

9. Which sentence tells someone to do something and ends with a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. Did you close the door?
   B. Close the door.
   C. The door is red
   D. What a big door!

10. What is a plough? (1 mark)
   A. A tool or machine used to turn over soil before planting
   B. A small insect that damages crops
   C. A place for storing tools
   D. A kind of fertilizer

11. How is the sound /v/ made? (1 mark)
   A. The upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes
   B. The lips are rounded and do not touch the teeth
   C. The tongue touches the roof and there is no voice
   D. The mouth is closed and air passes through the nose

12. What does it mean to read in phrases? (1 mark)
   A. To read groups of words that go together
   B. To read one letter at a time
   C. To read backwards
   D. To read only the first word of each line

13. 'It's' is a short form of which words? (1 mark)
   A. it was only
   B. it is or it has
   C. its own
   D. it will only

14. In which tense is a narrative usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Future tense
   B. Present progressive
   C. Command
   D. Past tense

15. How do we speak about people who are ill? (1 mark)
   A. By ignoring them
   B. With care and respect
   C. With fear
   D. With jokes

16. Which is a sign of good speaking fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Whispering so nobody hears
   B. Stopping after every word
   C. Speaking clearly at a steady pace
   D. Speaking as fast as possible

17. Which is NOT a way in which HIV spreads? (1 mark)
   A. Through blood
   B. Sitting together in class
   C. From a mother to her baby
   D. Sharing sharp objects that have blood on them

18. What should you do if you find a needle or razor blade on the ground? (1 mark)
   A. Give it to a younger child
   B. Pick it up and keep it
   C. Play with it
   D. Not touch it and tell a trusted adult

19. What does an adverb tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many things there are
   B. The name of a place
   C. A person's name
   D. More about a verb, such as how, when or where

20. Which sentence uses the right word for how she sings? (1 mark)
   A. She sings good.
   B. She sings well.
   C. She sing well.
   D. She sings goodly.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Compose a tongue twister with at least six words that contain the sound /w/. (3 marks)

22. Name the three parts of fluent reading and explain each briefly. (3 marks)

23. Write the short forms of: did not, she has, we will, let us. (4 marks)

24. Why did the teacher say the prize message might be a trick? (3 marks)

25. Write one statement, one WH question and one yes or no question about email. Say how the voice moves in each. (3 marks)

26. Write a title and an opening sentence for a story about a girl who finds a lost phone. (2 marks)

27. Explain the difference between 'good' and 'well'. Give one sentence for each. (4 marks)

28. Explain how /v/ and /w/ are made differently. (2 marks)

29. Describe the five-finger test for choosing a book. (4 marks)

30. Explain why 'more better' is wrong. Give the correct form. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — taller
   Short adjectives add er.

2. D — suddenly
   Time words show order.

3. C — the exciting part
   Events rise to an exciting part.

4. C — some
   Some is used in positive statements.

5. C — The last picture
   The last picture usually shows how it finished.

6. C — chair
   'Chair' ends with the /ɛə/ sound.

7. B — Kamau bought data bundles yesterday.
   'Bought' and 'yesterday' show the action is finished.

8. D — It helps you remember them
   Writing new words helps you remember them.

9. B — Close the door.
   Commands usually end with a full stop.

10. A — A tool or machine used to turn over soil before planting
   The plough breaks up soil ready for planting.

11. A — The upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes
   /v/ uses teeth and lip; /w/ uses rounded lips only.

12. A — To read groups of words that go together
   Chunking words into phrases makes reading smoother.

13. B — it is or it has
   It's = it is / it has.

14. D — Past tense
   Narratives tell what happened.

15. B — With care and respect
   People who are ill need care, not fear.

16. C — Speaking clearly at a steady pace
   Fluent speech is clear and steady.

17. B — Sitting together in class
   Ordinary contact such as sitting together does not spread HIV.

18. D — Not touch it and tell a trusted adult
   Sharp objects may carry germs.

19. D — More about a verb, such as how, when or where
   Adverbs answer how, when and where.

20. B — She sings well.
   'Well' is the adverb; 'good' is an adjective.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: We watched worms wriggle when the wind whistled.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a sentence, 1 for at least six /w/ words, 1 for making sense.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Accuracy: reading the words correctly. Speed: reading at a comfortable, not rushed pace. Expression: using the voice to show meaning and feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part explained.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: didn't, she's, we'll, let's
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: It promised a prize but asked for personal details, and some people send such messages to steal information.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for prize, 1 mark for details, 1 mark for stealing.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: I sent the email (falls). Where is the message? (falls) Did you get it? (rises)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with correct voice movement.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title: An Honest Girl. One morning, Achieng found a phone near the school gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: 'Good' is an adjective and describes a noun: She is a good singer. 'Well' is an adverb and describes a verb: She sings well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each sentence.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: For /v/ the upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes; for /w/ the lips are rounded and do not touch the teeth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open the book at a page and read it. Hold up a finger for every word you do not know. Five fingers means too hard; one to three fingers is a good fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reading a page, 1 for counting unknown words with fingers, 1 for what five fingers means, 1 for what one to three fingers means.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Better is already the comparative form, so we do not add more. The correct form is better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the reason and 1 mark for the correct form.
